summary: Glacier National Park's oldest surviving lookout, staffed by a married couple in 1949-1951 and last staffed around 1971.

facts.design: Two-story timber cab with short hip roof, one of three Glacier lookouts of this style

access.note: Reached by a 7-mile trail; no source confirms public entry is permitted

events.note: NHLR and firelookout.com give 1929; NHLR calls it the oldest remaining lookout in the park
Staffed by Raymond and Marie Matheny from 1949 to 1951, per an NPS photo caption
firelookout.com reports the lookout was staffed through 1971
Wrapped in fire-resistant material during the Sprague Fire

evidence.quote: One of three structures with a short hip roof, Mount Brown Lookout is the oldest remaining lookout in Glacier National Park. It was constructed in 1929. The lookout is reached by a 7-mile trail.
From 1949 to 1951, Mount Brown Lookout was manned by lookouts Raymond and Marie Matheny.
Built in 1929, this 2-story NPS cab with high hip roof was last staffed in 1971. The structure was rehabilitated in 1999 and is listed on the National Historic Lookout Register.
The low two-story timber-construction structure with a pyramidal roof was built in 1928.
Mount Brown Fire Lookout with fire resistant wrapping installed to help it withstand the Sprague Fire in 2017

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR and firelookout.com give 1929; Wikipedia's infobox gives 1928. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Good staffing detail (Mathenys, last staffed 1971) and a notable 2017 Sprague Fire protection event, but sources don't describe the fire's actual approach/outcome for the structure beyond the wrap being installed.
